FILE: research/audits/api_inputs/2026-11-13-jack-classical/jack-prefix-amplitude-sampler.md
One obligation: apply the ACTUAL Bravyi-Gosset-Liu amplitude-only sampling algorithm to the full Jack branching circuit, attempting an end-to-end classical sampler for unrestricted lambda. This is distinct from derivative-norm computation, commuting-charge elimination, and paired-map sampling. Source Algorithm2 needs polynomially many amplitudes of ALL circuit prefixes, not just final amplitudes. Its ground-state route needs a unique ground state, gap AND sensitivity bounds plus amplitude evaluation. Determine whether the explicit branching construction permits prefix amplitudes (including controlled polar QPE/simulation) to collapse to polynomially many computable corner/occupation quantities. At ideal inverse-branching block boundaries, remaining path records determine a subshape nu of the original lambda, and the quantum data is Jhat_nu; verify this observation and whether it actually makes prefix computation efficient. Do NOT declare individual Jack/Lax coefficients efficiently evaluable without a full algorithm. Nor may one assume a gapped local parent for arbitrary excited Jack lambda. First look for a complete constructive classical simulation using this actual state/circuit structure. If none, identify exactly the unpaid amplitude/gap/sensitivity object; a failure of one circuit contraction is not hardness. Avoid a generic source summary or recapitulating existing downset sampler. All D,epsilon and bit costs explicit. No tools/browsing; source excerpts are authoritative only at their stated scopes.


FILE: research/audits/api_inputs/2026-11-13-jack-classical/native-contract.md
Native question: given an explicit partition lambda of numerical degree D, fixed alpha=3, sample mu with Born probability theta_mu(lambda)^2 z_mu 3^length(mu)/H_lambda, where J_lambda=sum theta_mu p_mu and H_lambda is the integral Jack hook norm. Error TV epsilon. All arithmetic, precision, conditional probabilities, normalizers and rejection/mixing costs paid. No coefficient/partition-function oracle, no hidden quantum input. Existing exact classical algorithm costs poly(D)*M(lambda)^2 where M counts Young subshapes; bounded Durfee is already polynomial, unrestricted worst case exp(O(sqrt D)). A reviewed WRITTEN quantum clean full basis transform costs poly(D,1/epsilon) on Hall occupation basis; no novelty or separation follows. Need matched classical improvement for unrestricted shapes, not a new easy family or finite sweep.
Exact sampler reduction: for f initially J_lambda, choose k with weight ||3k partial_pk f||^2/(3d||f||^2), update f, repeat. Desired new result: compute/estimate these ADAPTIVE derivative norms in poly(D,1/epsilon) BIT without explicit downset. Any relative estimator must have uniform success and variance/mixing bounds on reached histories; exponentially rare events cannot be silently postselected.
Actual new source gives R_r=(-1)^r[t^r]exp(B_infty(t,p,-3r)), J_lambda=R_lambda1 ... R_lambdal 1. Gamma_Y and B_n are in primary excerpt. At b=2 all Gamma coefficients are nonnegative, but u=-3r is negative: formal positivity is NOT native positivity. Absolute path operator A_r=[t^r]exp(B_infty(t,p,+3r)) has positive coefficients. Parent provisional derivation from Cor5.3: A_D 1=binom(2D-1,D)J_(D), so a large one-row cancellation ratio alone does NOT refute normalized Born sampling. Check rather than assume this observation.
Reports are advisory, no tools/browsing. Prove material steps or mark OPEN. Do not cite unavailable source claims. No generic confirmation review or implementation plan. Give concrete mechanism, costs, strongest classical baseline, proof obligations/falsifier, and disposition of exactly what is established.

# 2026-11-13 — Independent coherent Jack branching construction

ACCEPT the written full transform at FIXED alpha=3, numerical degree D,
with a deterministic circuit of size poly(D,1/epsilon), 0<epsilon<1. On the valid shape
subspace it maps |mu>|0> to |Jhat_mu>|0> within epsilon in isometry/operator
norm, uniformly on arbitrary superpositions. Here the output coordinates
are the orthonormal power-sum occupations, not physical particle positions.
This is a proof of a native circuit construction, not an implementation,
novelty claim, classical lower bound, or demonstrated useful advantage.

The elementary principal-square-root compiler below pays the complete
precision clock. It does NOT claim poly(D,log(1/epsilon)); that stronger
precision dependence would need a separately checked phase-synthesis route.
No supplied Jack reflection, coefficient oracle, recursive state-preparation
inverse, measurement, postselection, or enumeration of partitions/paths is used.

Inputs checked: JACK_COHERENT_BRANCHING_TRANSFORM; the stable all-degree
intertwiner and overlap reviews; actual Mickler–Moll source. For simulation,
actual Aharonov–Ta-Shma quant-ph/0301023v2, retained `aharonov_tashma.txt`,
Lemma 1 and §5 (physical LF 855–1039) give constructive sparse simulation,
including clean 2-by-2 blocks and operator-norm error. Actual Gilyen et al.
1806.01838v1, `gilyen_qsvt.txt` 1640–1673, does supply positive singular-vector
transformation at the stated query cost; its phase compiler is unnecessary
for the weaker, completely explicit precision dependence proved here.

## 1. Exact positive branching coefficients

Let F_n be the degree-n power-sum space and H_d=F[w]_d. All basis vectors
below are normalized in the alpha=3 Hall inner product. Put d=n-1,
V=A_d^dagger/sqrt(3n), and write v_(lambda,s)=psi_(lambda,s)/||psi_(lambda,s)||.
The established identity A_d psi_(lambda,s)=J_(lambda+s) and AA^dagger=3n I
imply

    V Jhat_mu = sum_(r in R_mu) sqrt(q_mu,r) v_(mu-r,r),
    q_mu,r = ||J_mu||^2/[3n ||psi_(mu-r,r)||^2] > 0,
    sum_r q_mu,r=1.

These coefficients are POSITIVE, using pi0 psi=J and the positive norm.
No undetermined relative eigenvector phase remains. The q values can be
computed without evaluating a Jack polynomial: if a_i are addable contents
of mu and b_j=c(r_j)+2 its outer-corner contents, then

    q_mu,r_j = -Res_(u=b_j) 1/m_mu(u) /(3n),
    m_mu(u)=product_j(u-b_j)/product_i(u-a_i).

The residue is a product/quotient of O(n) nonzero integers of magnitude O(n).
Thus each rational has O(n log(n+1)) numerator/denominator bits before any
cancellation; exact prefix sums also have polynomial bits. The independent
bounds q>=1/n and tau>=3/(16d) for d>0 hold. The d=0 up overlap is one.

## 2. Global polar pairs, including content degeneracies

For a fixed content c let P_c be the GLOBAL spectral projector of L_d, and
let P0 be the marker-zero projector. The orthogonal cyclic decomposition
and simple spectrum inside each Z_lambda give the exact singular expansion

    P0 P_c = sum_(lambda: c in A_lambda)
               sqrt(tau_lambda,c) |Jhat_lambda><v_lambda,c|.

There is at most one corner of content c for any given lambda. The left
vectors are orthonormal across lambda, as are the right vectors. Hence this
is a genuine singular decomposition, despite global L_d degeneracies.
In particular every vector in the valid P_c image has nonzero singular value
at least 1/(4d) for d>=1, using the weaker tau>=1/(16d^2).

Let

    W_c=(2P0-I)(2P_c-I).

On one singular plane, write u=Jhat_lambda and
v=v_lambda,c=cos(theta)u+sin(theta)u_perp, where cos(theta)=sqrt(tau)>0.
In the ordered basis (u,u_perp),

    W_c = [[cos(2theta), sin(2theta)],[-sin(2theta), cos(2theta)]].

Its PRINCIPAL square root is the same rotation through half the angle,
so W_c^(1/2) v=u with positive coefficient one. If tau=1, the common line
has W_c=1 and the map is identity. For tau<1, the two eigenphases are
+-2theta and their distance from the principal-branch cut at -1 is

    pi-2theta=2 arcsin(sqrt(tau)) >= 2 sqrt(tau).

For every stage d<=D, the conservative rational lower bound

    g0=1/[2(D+1)]

therefore separates every REQUIRED eigenphase from the cut. Zero-singular
or P0-only blocks may have W_c=-1, but are outside the promised P_c input.
The algorithm below still defines a unitary circuit on them; no assertion
of approximation to a discontinuous square root on the whole ambient space
is needed. The required Jordan planes are mutually orthogonal and reduce
both native projectors.

## 3. A finite positive-polar compiler using ordinary coherent QPE

This section gives a uniform restricted-operator-norm error, not merely a
basis-state probability bound. To approximate the positive polar map within
zeta (0<zeta<1/2), set

    h=min(g0/4,zeta/4),  xi=zeta^2/64,
    M=the least power of two >=16/(xi h^2).

Apply ordinary coherent M-point phase estimation to W_c, interpret its
estimate phihat in [-pi,pi), apply the phase exp(i phihat/2) to the phase
register, and UNCOMPUTE phase estimation. The phase operation is elementary:
for estimate j, it is exp(i*pi*j/M), with an additional minus sign when
j>=M/2. It uses binary controlled one-qubit phases, not QSVT phase synthesis.

For a W_c eigenphase phi, let p_j be its QPE outcome probabilities. The exact
Dirichlet-kernel amplitude at circular angular distance a from phi is at
most pi/(M a). Therefore

    Pr(circular phase error>h) <= pi^2/(M h^2) <= xi.

This intentionally loose bound sums over all M bins; it already gives a
polynomial clock. On the good bins, h<g0 ensures no branch-cut crossing and
|exp(i phihat/2)-exp(i phi/2)|<=h/2. Uncomputation gives the EXACT identity

    ||U_polar(|omega>|0>)-exp(i phi/2)|omega>|0>||^2
      = sum_j p_j |exp(i phihat_j/2)-exp(i phi/2)|^2.

Thus the clean-vector error is at most h/2+2sqrt(xi)<=3zeta/8. The circuit
and ideal function are block diagonal in the W_c eigenspaces, so the same
bound is an OPERATOR NORM bound on their entire required direct sum. There
is no factor depending on its dimension. Controlled c blocks obey the same
maximum bound; the circuit never needs lambda or tau.

There are fewer than 2M controlled W_c calls including uncomputation.
Approximate each by operator error <=zeta/(32M), and allocate total error
<=zeta/8 to the ordinary QFT and half-phase gates. A hybrid bound gives total
error <zeta. All gates remain unitary, with no discarded failure history.
The phase workspace is within zeta of zero on every promised input.

Here M=poly(D,1/zeta); its register length and every angle precision are
O(log(D+1)+log(1/zeta)). Repeated powers of W_c are implemented by their
charged number of ordinary calls, not an unprovided fast-forwarding oracle.

use an explicit native decomposition here: split each mode-k chain according
to parity of the larger m_k into two disjoint edge matchings, and keep 2l
as the diagonal term. This gives 2d+1 terms, each composed of 1-by-1 or
2-by-2 blocks. Their total norm bound is <=8(D+1)^2. Reversible matching
labels are polynomial-time functions of the occupations and marker. Label
each pair by its higher-m_k endpoint and that endpoint's weight: the computed
metadata is identical at both endpoints and can be uncomputed after rotation.

and use R=ceil(260 Lambda^2/rho) first-order product-formula slices.
The unitary Duhamel bound is t^2 Lambda^2/(2R)<=rho/8. Approximate each of

another rho/8. Computing pi and the evolution time is included in the
remaining operator-error budget. Clean block-rotation synthesis follows.
This proves a fixed polynomial gate clock in D and 1/rho. Angles t*sqrt(3k m_k) and diagonal phases have polynomial
bit algorithms. Ordinary finite-universal-set one-qubit gate synthesis
adds polynomial overhead; all controlled versions have the same norm bounds.

their phases. Controlled gates are compiled directly or with tracked phase
corrections; an unknown block-dependent global phase cannot be dropped.
This also supplies a direct native specialization of the retained source.

    M0=2^ceil(log2(8(D+1))).

ordinary QFT gates with a total operator budget rho give a clean content

controlled versions of these circuits. The two global reflection signs are
fixed consistently so their product is exactly the W_c in §2.

The other native isometry is

    V|m> = sum_(k:m_k>0) sqrt(k m_k/n)|m-e_k,l=k-1>.

on the padded occupation registers; valid inputs never wrap. Prefix-tree
rotations have polynomially many branches and polynomial-bit weights.
All arithmetic is computed and uncomputed while m is available. This is
an explicit full unitary on padded registers with marker initially zero;
its inverse restores m before reversing the mode preparation. No supplied
inverse of a Jack preparation appears.

## 5. Clean B_n and C_n, including reversible label erasure

Define the ideal B_n as follows: apply V, coherently extract content c, and
apply the c-controlled positive polar map of §2. The marker is now zero,
and all auxiliary polar/content workspace is zero in the ideal map. Thus

    B_n: Jhat_mu |0> -> sum_r sqrt(q_mu,r) Jhat_(mu-r)|c(r)>.

All relative phases are positive: this follows separately from the native

principal-root calculation. Different content values are retained, not
silently merged under the many-to-one map A_d.

For C_n, from an explicit shape mu enumerate removable corners and compute

polynomial bit length; nonzero conditional probabilities are bounded below

Angle approximation and all workspace cleanup are therefore uniform over
all valid shapes, without enumerating their exponentially many possibilities.

Update (mu,c) to (mu-r(c),c). This map is injective on valid pairs: from
(lambda,c), the unique addable corner of content c reconstructs mu. Both

extension can be built by computing the forward map into a blank register,

    C_n: |mu>|0> -> sum_r sqrt(q_mu,r)|mu-r>|c(r)>

not assume that an arbitrary rectangular isometry has a free inverse.

even though isolated contents have global degeneracies.

Pad workspaces with zeros so both downward maps use a common vacuum/path

## 6. Uniform composition and final finite clock

There is a useful inverse-on-range bound. If two full unitaries U and Utilde
satisfy ||(Utilde-U)|S||<=a, then on U(S),

    ||(Utilde^dagger-U^dagger)U|S||
      = ||Utilde^dagger(U-Utilde)|S|| <= a.

Therefore forward approximation of each B construction on its promised
clean input already pays the use of its ACTUAL circuit inverse on the
corresponding path range. No global approximation to the polar square root

For D>=1 take zeta=epsilon/[16(D+1)]. Budget each B_n at <=4zeta and each

    6D zeta < epsilon.

Every bound is restricted OPERATOR norm: controlled arithmetic is a direct

# Classical Jack Born sampling on a partition down-set

13 November 2026. The completed 149-line advisory report was read in full.
The following is an unconditional classical algorithm at fixed alpha=3,
using the already source-checked one-box Pieri identity. Degree D is a
charged numerical parameter. No network, API, Git, or CAS sweep was used.
STATE/TRAPS and the retained primary formulas were checked; interpreter:
/opt/anaconda3/bin/python.

For a partition lambda of D, put

    S(lambda)={nu:nu subseteq lambda},    M=|S(lambda)|,
    H_nu=||J_nu||^2.

There is an exact expected-polynomial-time classical sampler for

    pi_lambda(mu)=theta_mu^2 z_mu 3^length(mu)/H_lambda,
    J_lambda=sum_mu theta_mu p_mu,

with cost poly(D)*M^2 on polynomial-bit integers. There is also a bounded
time sampler within TV error epsilon, costing poly(D,log(1/epsilon))*M^2.
This proves polynomial classical Born sampling for all bounded-Durfee
families. It is not a general polynomial sampler, a hardness result, or a
classical construction of the coherent coefficient state.

## 1. Exact derivative sampling identity

For homogeneous nonzero f of degree d, adjointness and Euler's identity give

    sum_(k=1)^d ||V_-k f||^2=3d||f||^2,
    V_-k=3k partial_(p_k),       V_k^dagger=V_-k.

Choose k with probability ||V_-k f||^2/(3d||f||^2), replace f by V_-k f,
and repeat until degree zero. Output the multiset of selected k's.
Zero-norm branches have probability zero and are excluded. Each selected
branch is nonzero; there are at most D selections.

Here is a direct proof of the output law. In the orthonormal power-sum
basis, V_-k takes |mu> to sqrt(3k*m_k(mu)) |mu-k>. For fixed k this map on
the supported basis labels is injective. The norm update therefore has
exactly the same distribution as first drawing mu from the Born law and
then repeatedly removing a part k with probability k*m_k(mu)/d. At the
end the recorded multiset is precisely that original mu. Equivalently,
the report's ordered-path telescoping proof gives the same law. Neither
argument assumes nonnegative Jack coefficients.

## 2. All required operators are computable inside S(lambda)

The hypothesis H_P in the report is now PAID:

    P J_nu:=V_1 J_nu=sum_s tau_(nu,s) J_(nu+s).

Actual sources: Mickler's follow-up Lemma 2.8, (43)--(44), and Stanley
Theorem 6.1 in the integral-Jack normalization; the weights agree with
Mickler--Moll (1.18). See also the independent Lax intertwiner review,
Section 1. No finite test is being substituted for Pieri.

Set E=sum_(b>=1) V_(b+1)V_-b. The source T3 formula and transfer eigenvalue
give

    [T3,V_1]=6E+6V_1,
    T3 J_nu=3(2 sum_(t in nu)c(t)+2|nu|)J_nu,
    E J_nu=sum_s c(s)tau_(nu,s)J_(nu+s),       c(x,y)=3x-y.

Also [E,V_k]=3k V_(k+1), so the raising matrices U_k for multiplication
by p_k are obtained by

    U_1=P,        U_(k+1)=(E U_k-U_k E)/(3k).                       (1)

Equivalently U_k=ad_E^(k-1)(P)/(3^(k-1)(k-1)!).

Restriction is exact. Every P/E word follows a chain of added boxes.
If its endpoints rho,kappa lie in S(lambda), every intermediate diagram
lies inside kappa and hence inside lambda. A path that leaves this down-set
cannot return. Thus the restricted recurrence gives the true coefficients
of p_k J_rho at every retained kappa; it also proves the containment support.

Adjointness then gives the lowering matrix

    [D_k]_(rho,kappa)=[U_k]_(kappa,rho) H_kappa/H_rho,
    D_k=diag(H)^(-1) U_k^T diag(H).                                (2)

It preserves the down-set. Starting with the vector e_lambda, compute
D_k f for every k<=d and their diagonal Hall norms, choose a branch by
Section 1, and retain its coefficient vector. Enumerating the down-set,
forming its one-box edges, and computing (1)--(2) uses polynomial work in
D and M. A safe, nonoptimized count is O(D^2 M^2) rational operations for
preprocessing and one complete sample: E is O(D)-sparse per row/column,
and there are at most D matrices, D selections, and D candidate k's.
No tight arithmetic-operation count from the report is needed.

## 3. An explicit polynomial-BIT bound

Assume D>=1; the empty partition is trivial. Define

    L=lcm(1,2,...,4D),          Q=L^(D^2+4D).

Computing L requires only integer gcd/lcm, not factoring. The elementary
bound log_2 L<=4D log_2(4D) suffices.

The ACTUAL norm formula, Stanley Theorem 5.8 / Mickler Proposition 3.1, is

    H_nu=prod_(b in nu) (3a(b)+l(b)+1)(3(a(b)+1)+l(b)).             (3)

Every factor is an integer in [1,4D]. Consequently H_nu divides L^(2D)
and 1<=H_nu<=(4D)^(2D). We do not compute norms by inverting the report's
path-DP quantity T_nu.

Every Pieri denominator is a product of at most D nonzero integer corner
differences, each of absolute value at most 4D. Thus P and E entries have
denominators dividing L^D. Since tau>=0 and sum_s tau=1 before restriction,

    ||P||_1<=1,       ||E||_1<=3D.

Induction in (1) gives

    denom(U_k) divides L^((D+2)k),
    ||U_k||_1 <= (2D)^(k-1)/(k-1)!.                               (4)

For the denominator claim, one multiplication by E adds exponent D and
division by 3k adds at most two more, since both 3 and k divide L.
For the norm claim, (1) multiplies the preceding bound by at most 2D/k.
These bounds also control every intermediate commutator product and sum.

For a derivative history k_1,...,k_j of total removed degree m<=D, the
diagonal norm factors in (2) TELESCOPE. Its coefficient at nu is

    f_nu=(H_lambda/H_nu)
          (U_(k_1)...U_(k_j))_(lambda,nu).                         (5)

By (3)--(5), every f_nu has denominator dividing
L^((D+2)m+2D), hence dividing Q, and

    |f_nu| <= (4D)^(2D)(2D)^m <= (4D)^(3D).

The same bounds hold for EVERY candidate vector D_k f considered while
sampling, because its total removed degree is still at most D. Thus no
sequence of rational divisions can hide exponential intermediate height.

Writing f_nu=a_nu/Q, its Hall norm is

    ||f||^2=Q^(-2) sum_nu a_nu^2 H_nu.

There are M<=sum_(d=0)^D p(d)<=2^D summands. Numerators, denominators,
matrix entries, norms, and conditional probabilities therefore require
O(D^3 log(D+1)) bits. This is a proved coarse bound, replacing the report's
unsupported O(D^2.5)-bit estimate. Standard exact integer/rational
arithmetic makes the operation count in Section 2 polynomial BIT time.

## 4. Exact versus bounded-clock sampling

Clearing the common norm denominator gives exact nonnegative integer
transition weights with polynomial bit length. Uniform-integer rejection
sampling implements each transition exactly, with fewer than two expected
trials. This gives the exact expected-polynomial-time sampler.

A deterministic polynomial clock with TV guarantee is even simpler. At
each step use

    b=ceil(log_2(2D^2/epsilon))

fair bits to choose U uniformly from {0,...,2^b-1}/2^b and compare it with
the EXACT cumulative rational probabilities. Couple this to a continuous
uniform U before rounding. At most D cumulative boundaries can change the
choice, so conditional error is at most D/2^b. Over at most D adaptive
steps the total TV error is at most D^2/2^b<=epsilon. Empty intervals are
skipped, so a zero-norm branch is never selected. The bit count is
O(D(log D+log(1/epsilon))); arithmetic precision is the previous bound
plus O(log(1/epsilon)). Arbitrary rational probabilities cannot in general
be sampled exactly with a fixed finite number of fair bits, so these two
clock statements should remain distinct.

## 5. Shape scope and report corrections

If h is the Durfee-square size of lambda, every box of lambda lies in its
first h rows or first h columns. Recording those h row lengths and h column
heights determines any nu subseteq lambda. Hence

    M <= (D+1)^(2h).

All bounded-h families have polynomial classical Born samplers, including
hooks and bounded-row/column families. For h=(log D)^O(1), this algorithm
has a quasipolynomial upper bound. That DOES NOT exclude a possible
polynomial-versus-quasipolynomial quantum advantage. The report's asserted
requirement h=(log D)^omega(1) for ANY advantage is rejected. The correct
comparison is against poly(D)*M^O(1) on the actual target family; some
additional families can have small M without bounded h.

The general upper bound M<=sum_(d<=D)p(d)=exp(O(sqrt(D))) remains useful,
but its maximizing constant is irrelevant to this result. No general
sampler or hardness follows from the cost of this representation. The
degree-12/14 sweeps and worst-case-constant project recommended in the
report are unnecessary and are not queued. A polynomial native method
for the required derivative norms at unrestricted shapes would still
change the general comparison; this review supplies no such method.
